title: Skating Warm Up 01 – Forwards
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 04, 05
description: Set players up in two lines on the hashmarks. Send both lines together or alternate them, skating down the middle to the far end and returning along the boards. Players do each forward skating skill as diagrammed.
coaching_points: Focus on technique so players get plenty of quality skating reps.

title: Puck Control Warm Up 03 – Puck Dots
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 04
description: Set players up in two lines on the hashmarks. Lay out pucks or pylons in one or two straight rows down the ice. Send both lines together or alternate them, going down the middle to the far end and back along the boards. Players do each puck skill as diagrammed.
coaching_points: Stress technique.
Lots of pucks lets players repeat the same move many times.

title: Transition Races
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01
description: Make two lines, each with two pylons set one above the other. Players begin at the bottom pylon and, on the coach's signal, race to the top pylon, pivot, and skate backward to the bottom pylon. On the next rep, pivot the other way.
coaching_points: Make efficient turns that throw as little snow as possible.
Quick feet.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 01; this drill is the first station listed.

title: 4 Pylon Agility
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 04
description: Put 4 pylons around a circle or anywhere on the ice. Players carry a puck and stickhandle around the pylons in any order. Progressions: add a second player and have them challenge each other rather than avoid each other; then two players share one puck, facing each other and passing back and forth for support; then one player stays on the wall as a passer while the other skates and passes or plays one touch.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving, be creative, and go full speed with quick feet and hands.
Always be ready to give and take a pass; expect the puck.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 01; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Corner Puck Protect
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 04
description: Players start in the corner with pucks. Set a couple of obstacles at the top of the circle to mimic a defender's stick, such as a stick on a pylon or an assistant coach. Players open up and shield the puck as they go past the obstacle, then finish with a shot on net. Switch corners so both forehand and backhand sides get work.
coaching_points: Open up with a heel-to-heel move.
Pull the puck back toward the back foot to protect it as you open up.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 01; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Agility – 5 Puck Agility
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 03
description: Set 5 pucks in a circle pattern as diagrammed. Players skate around an outside puck, return to the middle, then go around another outside puck, always coming back to the centre in between. Keep toes pointed forward during transitions. Add a puck as a progression.
coaching_points: Quick feet and stay low for balance.
Be efficient, aiming for a single crossover back to the middle.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 01; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Quick Release – Shoot on Front Foot
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 01, 02
description: Players start in opposite corners, right-handed shots in one and left-handed shots in the other. Each player skates around the top of the circle and takes a pass from the opposite corner.
coaching_points: Take the pass across the body.
In one motion bring the puck to the forehand and shoot off the front foot.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 01; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Skating Warm Up – Backwards 01
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Set players up in two lines on the hashmarks. Send both lines together or alternate them, skating down the middle to the far end and returning along the boards. Players do each backward skating skill as diagrammed.
coaching_points: Focus on technique so players get plenty of quality skating reps.

title: Puck Control Warm Up 01
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Set players up in two lines on the hashmarks. Send both lines together or alternate them, skating down the middle to the far end and returning along the boards. Players do each puck skill as diagrammed.
coaching_points: Focus on technique and get as many reps of each skill as possible on the way down the ice.
Push for quick hands and a big range of motion.

title: Transition Footwork
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Set two pylons in a line. The player goes forward from the bottom pylon to the top one, pivots, and skates backward to the opposite side of the bottom pylon. Then pivot, skate forward on that same side to the top pylon, pivot again, and skate backward to the start. Progression: add a puck.
coaching_points: Quick feet.
Accelerate into and out of each pivot and keep your speed.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 02; this drill is the first station listed.

title: 3 Puck Stickhandle
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Set 3 pucks in a triangle anywhere on the ice. Keeping the feet still, players use only their arms and upper body to move a puck randomly around and between the 3 stationary pucks. Progression: spread the pucks wider and have players skate through them while stickhandling.
coaching_points: Quick hands and a full range of motion.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 02; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Crosby Delay
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Players start in the corner, skate up the wall, make a tight turn toward the boards, and use quick feet off the wall to attack the net. Set a couple of obstacles at the top of the circle to act as a defender's stick, such as a stick on a pylon or an assistant coach.
coaching_points: Check the glass or look over your shoulder before coming out of the turn to see what is there.
Accelerate out of the turn.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 02; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Circle Shooting
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02
description: Put pucks and players on both faceoff dots. A pass comes across from the opposite dot, and each player may skate either direction around the circle. The player without the puck gets into shooting position while the puck carrier finds that shooter and passes for the shot.
coaching_points: Quick feet around the circle.
Talk and call for the puck.
Make a good pass and release the shot quickly.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 02; this drill is the first station listed.

title: Corner Obstacle Agility
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 02, 05
description: Players start in the corner with pucks. Set a couple of obstacles in the circle to act as a defender's stick, such as a stick on a pylon or an assistant coach. Players make random moves, shifting the puck side to side and changing direction with quick feet and quick hands.
coaching_points: Let players solve it themselves and be creative.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 02; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Skating Warm Up – Forwards 02

title: Puck Control Warm Up 02 – Random Obstacles
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03, 05
description: Set players up in two lines on the hashmarks. Scatter lots of pucks randomly down the middle of the ice. Send both lines together or alternate them, going down the middle to the far end and back along the boards. Players do each puck skill as diagrammed.

Encourage creativity and quick hands.

title: End Wall Retrieval – Attack Net
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03
description: Keep pucks in the middle of the ice near the blue line with players lined up beside the coach. The coach dumps a puck in wide of the net. The player retrieves it and attacks the net.
coaching_points: Shoulder check and sell a fake before picking up the puck.
Quick feet out of the corner and drive the net with speed.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 03; this drill is the first station listed.

title: 1 Touch Pass and Move
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03, 05
description: Station one passer at the top of the circle and one at the bottom. A skater circles and exchanges passes with each stationary player, always facing the passer with the stick ready, then changes direction. Progressions: add a second one-touch pass, then add a second skater so two players circle at once.
coaching_points: Have the stick in position to receive.
Always face the passer and never turn your back on the puck.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 03; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Side Wall Retrieval – Attack Net
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03, 04
description: Players and pucks start in the middle of the ice. The coach passes a puck to the side wall, and the player chases it down, picks it up, and drives hard to the net. Players may pivot after the pickup to help protect the puck.
coaching_points: Turn your head toward the pivot to see what is there.
Pivot quickly and attack the net with speed.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 03; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Transition Footwork Races
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03
description: Set two pylons in a line. Players go forward from the bottom pylon to the top one, pivot, and skate backward to the opposite side of the bottom pylon. Then pivot, skate forward on that side to the top pylon, pivot again, and skate backward to the start. Progression: add a puck.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 03; this drill is the first station listed.

title: Quick Feet – Pass off Wall – Random
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 03
description: Pucks sit at the blue line with players lined up toward the corner. Players skate into the neutral zone, turn toward the boards, bank the puck off the boards, collect it, and attack the blue line with speed. At the obstacle, they deliberately miss the puck, let it slide past the obstacle, and pick it up on the far side.
coaching_points: Sell a head or shoulder fake.
Slide the stick off or over the puck to deceive the defender.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 03; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Skating Circles
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 04
description: Players line up in the corner. They perform skating skills around both circles so each skill is done equally in both directions. Skills: crossunders, C-cuts, quick-feet hi-lo's, heel-to-heel back-foot push, heel-to-heel open up, and inside pivot with one crossover.
coaching_points: Get the technique right before adding speed.
Repeat each skill as often as needed until the footwork is correct.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 04; this drill is the first station listed.

title: Agility Nets (Skating)
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 04
description: Set a net in the neutral zone or anywhere on the ice as a station. Players use skating techniques around it to build quickness, agility, and creativity. Add a second player to work on heads-up play or to act as a defender so both offence and defence are practised.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 04; this drill is the second station listed.

title: Eberle Move
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 04
description: Pucks are on the boards at the blue line, with an obstacle or coach at the top of the circle and a second near the bottom. The player skates at the obstacle with the puck on one side of the stick, pulls it back, then pushes it forward on the other side of the stick.
coaching_points: Quick hands; the forward-back-forward motion opens a shooting lane.
Changing the puck's angle gives a better chance to beat the goalie.

title: Transition Skating
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 05
description: Put 4 pylons around a circle or anywhere on the ice. From the bottom of the circle, players skate forward to a top pylon, pivot backward to a lower pylon, pivot forward to the top pylon on the other side, pivot backward to the other lower pylon, then pivot forward to the top of the circle, stop, and skate forward back to the start. Add a puck as a progression.
coaching_points: Quick feet.
Keep your speed coming out of each pivot.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 05; this drill is the first station listed.

title: Crosby Behind the Net
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 05
description: Players start in opposite corners with pucks. They skate behind the net and, at the far post, make a tight turn or open up into a heel-to-heel turn. Protect the puck to shake a defender and create a scoring chance.

coaching_points: Sell the fake first.
Move the puck quickly from forehand to backhand or backhand to forehand.
station_note: Diagram shows all three stations from Plan 05; this drill is the third station listed.

title: Skating Agility Warm Up
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 06
description: Players do crossovers into slide stops, both forward and backward. They work in a zig-zag pattern through the middle lane.
coaching_points: Keep a deep knee bend.
Stay balanced through the slide stops.
Quick feet.

Stay in control at a fast pace.

Get into a shooting lane quickly.
Shoot in stride.
Keep your eyes on the target.

source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 06

Be creative.
Quick feet and quick hands.

title: Half Wall 1 on 1
source_collection: Hockey Canada Drill Hub · Sample Practice Plan 06
description: Players line up on the half wall at the hash marks. The offensive player carries a puck, touches the blue line, then turns to attack the net. The defender touches the goal line, then steps up to close the gap and play the 1 on 1.

Use an inside-out path.
Defender: stick on stick, stick on puck.
Close the gap as fast as possible.

Open the hips to turn your back to the defender quickly.

title: Organize and Basic Stance
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Organize and Basic Stance: Bring players to the centre ice circle and go over safety rules and signals. Explain and show the key points of the basic stance, then have players get into it while coaches move through the group correcting them. Players hop on both skates, lean left then right, balance on the left skate then the right, and rock forward to the toes and back to the heels to find their best balance point.
coaching_points: Coaches circulate and correct stance right away.
Help players find their best balance point.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Safety Rules, Basic Stance, Getting Up & Balance, Basic Knowledge, T-Push, C-Cuts

title: T-Push · Free Skate · Gettting Up and Balance
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: T-Push: Review and demonstrate the key points, then line players up along a line or the boards. With the right skate behind the left to form a T, they push down and out with the right while gliding on the left, fully extending and finishing with the toe; they push one foot at a time the full length of the zone, then switch feet. Free Skate: Players skate around the neutral zone to get comfortable, with coaches skating among them, chatting and helping as needed. Gettting Up and Balance: The coach shows how to get up properly, then plays Simon Says, having players drop to their knees and return to stance and touch knees, toes, head, shoulders, hips and so on. Players also lie on their stomachs with two hands on a level stick and elbows on the ice, pull up to their knees using the elbows, then stand, and the game continues.
coaching_points: Fully extend the pushing leg before recovering it.
Coaches watch each player and fix flaws individually.
Help players feel comfortable on their skates.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Safety Rules, Basic Stance, Getting Up & Balance, Basic Knowledge, T-Push, C-Cuts

title: Don’t Wake the Giant · C-Cuts · Fetch
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Don’t Wake the Giant: Scatter some pucks on the ice as treasure, guarded by a coach playing a giant who keeps dozing off. Players tiptoe past to steal the treasure without waking him, and the giant wakes now and then to chase them away. C-Cuts: Review and demonstrate the key points, then have players line up along the boards and do C-cuts across the ice with the right foot while gliding on the left. Do 3-4 reps with the right foot, then switch to the left. Fetch: Players are dogs and play without sticks; the coach rolls out one tennis ball per player, and players chase a ball, pick it up, and bring it back, barking when they return it. Some players may fetch 2-3 times while others fetch once.
coaching_points: Make sure players recover properly on each C-cut.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Safety Rules, Basic Stance, Getting Up & Balance, Basic Knowledge, T-Push, C-Cuts

title: Tour Bus
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Tour Bus: Split players into one group per coach. The coach drives the bus and players are passengers, following as the coach moves slowly around the area and changes direction often. Point out rink features along the way, such as the faceoff dot, circle, net, crease, blue line, centre line, and goal line. Return to those spots and have players name them.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Safety Rules, Basic Stance, Getting Up & Balance, Basic Knowledge, T-Push, C-Cuts

title: Free Skate (U7 Plan 2)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: Free Skate: Players skate clockwise. Between the blue lines they touch their knees, get into a sitting position, touch their toes, and speed up. Run it with or without pucks.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Falling Down, Gliding 2 foot, Gliding 1 Foot

title: Getting Up/Basic Stance · Balance and Agility · C-Cuts
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: Getting Up/Basic Stance: Review the key points for stance and getting up. Players lie on their backs and, on a signal, roll to their stomachs, get to their knees, and stand in the basic skating position, 4-5 times. Then from the goal line they take a few strides, drop to their knees, get up, and skate to the blue line, and repeat. Balance and Agility: Play Simon Says with balancing on one foot, jumping on one foot, jumping on two feet, and dropping to the knees and returning to stance. C-Cuts: Review and demonstrate the key points, then players line up along the boards or a line and do C-cuts across the ice with the right foot while gliding on the left, 3-4 reps, then switch to the left foot.
coaching_points: Make sure players recover properly on each C-cut.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Falling Down, Gliding 2 foot, Gliding 1 Foot

title: Fall Down · Gliding 2 Foot, 1 Foot · T-Push
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: Fall Down: Review and demonstrate the two falling safety rules, hands out and heads up when falling forward and tuck the chin when falling backward, and have players practise falling backward. Then they skate across, slide on their stomachs with hands out and heads up, get up and continue; repeat with a slide, roll over, get up and continue. Gliding 2 Foot, 1 Foot: Review and demonstrate the two-foot glide; from the boards players take a few strides, glide on both skates in basic stance, and repeat, also rising from stance to upright and back while gliding. For the one-foot glide, players balance on one foot then the other while leaning on the boards, then without the boards, then take a few strides and glide as far as they can on one skate before switching. T-Push: Review the key points and have players show their T for correction, then from the goal line in T-push position see how far each player goes on one push on the signal, with three attempts before switching feet.
coaching_points: Falling forward: hands out, heads up.
Falling backward: tuck the chin so the head stays off the ice.
Hold the basic stance while gliding.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Falling Down, Gliding 2 foot, Gliding 1 Foot

title: British Bulldog (U7)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2, 19
description: British Bulldog: Players start on the side boards and try to skate across to the other boards. Coaches begin as bulldogs and tag players as they pass. Anyone tagged becomes a bulldog for the next crossing. The last player tagged wins, and play continues until time runs out.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Falling Down, Gliding 2 foot, Gliding 1 Foot

title: Free Skate (U7 Plan 3)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3, 4
description: Free Skate: Players skate in a clockwise direction. Between the blue lines they drop to their knees and get up, glide on one foot, jump over the lines, and speed up. Add pucks if you like.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce Edge Control, One O’Clock – Eleven O’Clock Stop, Scooting

title: Edge Control · Obstacle Course · Scooting
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Edge Control: Set pucks along a quarter of a faceoff circle as diagrammed. Players take 4-5 strides, then glide on the inside edge of the left skate around the whole path without putting the right skate down, and line up on the other side. They come back on the outside edge of the left skate, then repeat everything on the right skate. Obstacle Course: Review and demonstrate the two falling safety rules, hands out and heads up going forward and tuck the chin going backward, and set out sticks and pylons as diagrammed. Players go over the first stick, spread their skates at the second, go over the third, and slide on their stomachs under the obstacle; coming back they go around the pylons, over the sticks, and slide under the obstacle again. Scooting: Review and demonstrate the key points, then line players up along a line or the boards with the right skate behind the left in a T. They push down and out with the right while gliding on the left, extending fully and finishing with the toe, pushing one foot at a time the full distance before switching feet.
coaching_points: Falling forward: hands out, heads up; falling backward: tuck the chin.
Fully extend the pushing leg before recovering it.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce Edge Control, One O’Clock – Eleven O’Clock Stop, Scooting

title: C-Cuts Alternating · One O’clock – Eleven O’clock Stop
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: C-Cuts Alternating: Review and demonstrate the key points, then line players up along the boards or a line to do C-cuts on alternating feet. One O’clock – Eleven O’clock Stop: Teach it in three steps. First, the two-foot glide: from the goal line, players take a few strides and glide on both skates in basic stance while coaches correct flaws. Second, making snow: standing still, players turn the right heel out and toe in and push the skate down and out to build a pile of snow, then the left, 3 times per skate for about 15 seconds. Third, a dry run standing still: glide in basic stance, unweight and turn one foot while gliding on the other, then lean on it.
coaching_points: Bring the foot back to the middle of the body before cutting with the other foot.
Hold the basic stance during the glide.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce Edge Control, One O’Clock – Eleven O’Clock Stop, Scooting

title: Cops and Robbers
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Cops and Robbers: Coaches are the cops and players are robbers who scatter around the zone without sticks. A tagged player goes to jail, either the net or the referee's circle. A free player can release someone from jail by tagging them. The goal is to have every player in jail by the end.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce Edge Control, One O’Clock – Eleven O’Clock Stop, Scooting

title: Edge Control · Striding
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Edge Control: Set pucks along a quarter of a faceoff circle as diagrammed. Players take 4-5 strides, then glide on the inside edge of the left skate around the whole path without putting the right skate down, and line up on the other side. They return on the outside edge of the left skate, then repeat on the right skate. Striding: Step 1 is scooting, with players on a line or the boards in a T, pushing down and out with the right skate while gliding on the left, going the full distance one foot at a time and returning on the other foot. Step 2 is alternating feet: after a review and demo, players start in basic stance on the goal line and on the signal push and recover with one skate and then the other, and repeat.
coaching_points: Extend the leg fully and finish the push with the toe before recovering.
Keep the recovery low to the ice.
Keep the glide foot under the body, not out to the side.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Striding, Glide Turns, Glide – Arm Pump

title: Gliding – Arm Pump · C-Cuts Alternating · One O’clock – Eleven O’clock Stop
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Gliding – Arm Pump: Review and demonstrate the key points, then line players up on the goal line. On the signal they pump their arms to drive themselves forward. C-Cuts Alternating: After a review and demo, players line up along the boards or a line and do C-cuts on alternating feet. One O’clock – Eleven O’clock Stop: Step 1, from the goal line players take a few strides and glide on two skates in basic stance while coaches correct flaws. Step 2, standing still they turn the right heel out and toe in and push down and out to make a pile of snow, then the left, 3 times each for about 15 seconds. Step 3 is a standing dry run: glide in basic stance, unweight and turn one foot while gliding on the other, then lean on it.
coaching_points: Bring the foot back to the middle of the body before the next C-cut.
Hold the basic stance during the glide.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Striding, Glide Turns, Glide – Arm Pump

title: Fun Time (U7 Plan 4)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Fun Time: Play cross-ice soccer. Players do not use sticks.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Striding, Glide Turns, Glide – Arm Pump

title: Tag (U7 Plan 5)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 5
description: Tag: Players skate anywhere on the ice while coaches are it and try to tag them. A tagged player goes to the Skill Doctor at the referee's circle, who gives them a skill to do before rejoining. Suggested tasks are dropping to the knees and getting up, balancing on one foot, and jumping on one foot. Play with or without pucks.

Shooting and Scoring: On each side of the ice lay a long stick across two pylons near the hash marks and put a pylon just short of the blue line, leaving half the pucks near the tops of the circles. Players skate toward the blue line, slide on their stomachs under the stick, get back up, tight turn around the pylon, skate to the net, pick up a puck, and score before returning to line.

title: Follow the Leader · V-Start and Tight Turns · Cops and Robbers
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 16
description: Follow the Leader: Challenge players with a series of tasks: jumping on one foot, gliding with a knee bend, gliding with an arm pump, lateral crossovers, gliding backward on one skate, 360s, and three quick crossovers left and right. title: One Foot Stop · Two Leg Backward Stop · 360’s

description: One Foot Stop: Review and demonstrate, then set pylons halfway between the goal line and blue line and split players into a group per pylon. title: Piggy Bank Race · V-Start/Tight Turns · Tag
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 20
description: Piggy Bank Race: Split into teams kneeling in a line beside their box, crate, or pail (the piggy bank), where a small opening is better because it forces a stop. Each team has the same number of pucks (coins) spread across the ice; on the signal the first player races out, does a one-foot stop, grabs a puck, returns, stops, and drops it in the bank before the next player goes. V-Start/Tight Turns: Review and demonstrate the front start and tight turns; in pairs with one pylon per pair halfway across, the first player opens into a V, takes 4-5 running strides to the pylon, tight turns around it, and returns for the partner, continuously, with the turn direction switched halfway and coaches correcting form. Then run it as a relay counting each team's correct tight turns within a time limit, and repeat turning the other way. Tag: Play Toilet Bowl Tag without sticks, with players skating around the end zone with hands on their knees while coaches tag them; tagged players stand with an arm out until a teammate skates under it, stops, and pushes it down.

title: Backwards Crossovers · Pivots Forward to Backward & Backward to Forward · Weaving with the Puck
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 26
description: Backwards Crossovers: Players do crossovers two and a half times around circle 1, then twice around circle 2. Send 2-3 players at a time and repeat 2-3 times. Pivots Forward to Backward & Backward to Forward: After a review, split into two groups positioned as diagrammed. Group 1 skates backward to a pylon, pivots backward to forward, accelerates out, two-foot stops at the boards, and joins group 2, with the next player leaving at the halfway point; group 2 skates forward to the pylon, pivots forward to backward, skates backward to the boards, V-stops, and joins group 1, with the next player leaving when the first reaches the pylon. Weaving with the Puck: Players weave a puck through the pylons, glide turn at the last one, skate forward 10 metres, and stop facing the boards. They then skate backward to the other side of the rink while controlling the puck.
coaching_points: Accelerate out of the pivot.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Use of feet to control the puck and puckhandling combinations

title: Tight Turns · Control Puck with Feet · Chaos
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 26
description: Tight Turns: Set pylons in two groups as diagrammed. Players race through them for a placed puck and finish with a shot on goal, adding a second puck for a second player if needed. Control Puck with Feet: Players cross the ice controlling the puck only with their feet, keeping it at their feet the whole way. Chaos: Each player skates randomly through the zone with a puck while coaches apply checking pressure. Players stickhandle on one leg, narrow-wide combined, side-front-side, switching hands, and with toe drags.
coaching_points: Keep the head up under pressure.
session_objectives: 1. Introduce: Use of feet to control the puck and puckhandling combinations

title: Warm Up (U7 Plan 27)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: Warm Up: Each skater gets a puck, tennis ball, or street hockey ball when they step on the ice and skates in any direction. On the whistle, they trade for a different item. No shooting, only puck control: stickhandle narrow-wide combined, side-front-side, through the legs, pulling the puck through the legs, and toe drags.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Starting and skating with the puck, open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving, pivots

title: Stationary Passing and Receiving · Weave with Puck · Puck Dots
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: Stationary Passing and Receiving: After a review and demo, partners stand about six metres apart. They pass on the forehand and receive on the backhand, then pass on the backhand and receive on the forehand. Weave with Puck: Players weave around staggered pylons, but instead of carrying the puck around each one, they slip it inside and pick it up after skating around the pylon. Puck Dots: Line up pucks as diagrammed. Straddling the row with their skates, players stickhandle back and forth through the puck dots.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Starting and skating with the puck, open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving, pivots

title: Mohawk on Circles · Stationary Stickhandling · Stopping with the Puck
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: Mohawk on Circles: Players start in the corner and on the coach's signal do forward crossovers around the circle. At the top and bottom of each circle they lift the inside foot, rotate it 180 degrees, and set it down heels facing each other, then lift and rotate the other foot 180 degrees so the feet are parallel again. Stationary Stickhandling: Players line up in stickhandling position with two pucks and stickhandle both. Stopping with the Puck: After a review and demo, players start on the wall, skate across the ice with a puck, and stop at the far wall.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Starting and skating with the puck, open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving, pivots

title: British Bull Dog
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: British Bull Dog: Players start at one end with a puck each, and the instructor stands at centre ice as the bulldog. Players skate to the other end with their pucks while the bulldog tries to knock pucks away. A player who loses their puck joins the instructor at centre ice as another bulldog.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Starting and skating with the puck, open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving, pivots

title: Warmup (U7 Plan 28)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Warmup: Players skate freely doing stops and starts while keeping control of the puck. They stickhandle narrow-wide combined, side-front-side, through the legs, pulling the puck through the legs, and with toe drags.
coaching_points: Keep control of the puck through stops and starts.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Mohawk pivots, Lead pass, Open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving

title: Passing and Receiving · Passing and Receiving · Mohawk on Circles
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Passing and Receiving: In groups of 4-5, one leader faces the others, who fan out in front, and the puck goes back and forth; rotate the leader often and have players receive on the forehand and pass on the backhand, then switch. Passing and Receiving: In groups of three, a player takes a pass, does a turn, drops to a knee, gets back up and passes to a partner. Mohawk on Circles: From the corner on the coach's signal, players do forward crossovers around the circle. At the top and bottom of each circle they lift the inside foot, turn it 180 degrees and set it down heel-to-heel, then lift and turn the other foot so the feet are parallel again.
coaching_points: Rotate the leader often so everyone passes and receives.
Work both forehand and backhand for passing and receiving.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Mohawk pivots, Lead pass, Open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving

title: Lead Pass · Skate and Pass · Pairs Passing
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Lead Pass: Demonstrate the key points and set up the course from the diagram; on the signal O2 and O3 skate out with sticks on the ice while O1 and O4 lead them so the puck arrives about five metres out. O2 carries around the pylon and joins the O4 line, O1 joins the O2 line and O3 joins O1. Skate and Pass: Two lines face each other about 20 metres apart with a passing spot painted about 4 metres in front of each line; the leader of line A carries to the spot, passes to the leader of line B and skates to the back of line B, and the receiver repeats it the other way. Pairs Passing: Pylons are set across the rink about three metres apart with one row of players on each side, and players finish at the back of the opposite line.
coaching_points: Receivers keep the stick on the ice, ready for the pass.
Lead the skater so the puck meets them in stride.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Mohawk pivots, Lead pass, Open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving

title: Pond Hockey (U7 Plan 28)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28, 31
description: Pond Hockey: Play across the ice in three areas with a puck and pylons for goals. A goal counts only when the puck hits the pylon. Teams must make three passes before they can score. There are no goalies.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Mohawk pivots, Lead pass, Open ice carry, weaving with the puck, passing/receiving

title: Freeze Tag
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: Freeze Tag: One player is it while everyone else skates around with a puck trying to avoid being tagged. When the tagger comes close, a player is safe only by standing completely still with the puck under control. Play until everyone is frozen. You can have more than one tagger at a time.
coaching_points: Players must keep the puck under control to be safe.
session_objectives: Review: Starting and stopping with puck, open ice carry, passing/receiving while moving, wrist shot, puckhandling, pivots

title: Stationary Passing · Puck Dots · Pairs Passing
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: Stationary Passing: Partners stand about 5-6 metres apart, each with a puck, and pass to each other at the same time. Puck Dots: Lay out a row of pucks as diagrammed; players straddle the row and stickhandle side to side through the dots. Pairs Passing: Partners skate around the zone passing the puck back and forth.
session_objectives: Review: Starting and stopping with puck, open ice carry, passing/receiving while moving, wrist shot, puckhandling, pivots

title: Wrist Shot – Forehand · Moving Puck Control – Sticks · Crossovers
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: Wrist Shot – Forehand: After a demonstration, each player stands still with a puck about 3-4 metres from the boards and shoots at a spot on the boards. Moving Puck Control – Sticks: Lay two sticks parallel and have players stickhandle forward and backward through them in a Z pattern. Crossovers: Players do crossovers around a circle, always facing the same direction.
session_objectives: Review: Starting and stopping with puck, open ice carry, passing/receiving while moving, wrist shot, puckhandling, pivots

title: Warm Up (U7 Plan 30)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30, 31, 32
description: Warm Up: Players skate freely doing stops and starts while keeping control of the puck. Mix in stickhandling moves: narrow-wide combination, side-front-side, stick through the legs, pulling the puck through the legs and toe drags.
coaching_points: Keep control of the puck through every stop and start.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s, passing/receiving while moving, bank pass, wrist shot, Tight turns

title: Wrist Shot – Forehand · Balance and Agility · Moving Puck Control – Figure 8’s
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30
description: Wrist Shot – Forehand: After a demonstration, each player stands still with a puck about 3-4 metres from the boards and shoots at a spot on the boards. Balance and Agility: From the boards on the coach's signal, players cross the ice doing balance skills such as one-skate glides forward and backward, glides with knee bend, lateral crossovers and gliding arm pumps. Moving Puck Control – Figure 8's: Players skate a figure 8 around pylons, cupping the puck around each one; going forward on the backhand the top-hand arm and elbow stay high, and on the forehand the arms cross over to help tighten the turn.
coaching_points: Keep the top-hand elbow high when carrying on the backhand.
Cross the arms over on the forehand to tighten the turn.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s, passing/receiving while moving, bank pass, wrist shot, Tight turns

title: Pairs Passing · Tight Turns · Skate-Pass-Shoot
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30
description: Pairs Passing: Partners pass in pairs and finish with a shot on net, then go to opposite corners to pick up a puck and come back to the opposite lines, making one pass off the boards on the way back. Tight Turns: Groups line up along the side boards with a pylon 15 metres out; the first player carries the puck around the pylon and passes to the next player, who does the same, going both directions around the pylon. Skate-Pass-Shoot: Players pass in groups of three and return to the line on their left.
coaching_points: Turn around the pylon in both directions.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s, passing/receiving while moving, bank pass, wrist shot, Tight turns

title: Baseball (U7)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30
description: Baseball: Split into two teams, using up to three areas. The batter has two pucks at home plate: one is shot into the field and the other is stickhandled around the four bases and home. Fielders get the shot puck, carry it to first, second or third base and pass it to the instructor at catcher; if the puck beats the batter home, the batter is out. Everyone bats once, then the teams switch.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s, passing/receiving while moving, bank pass, wrist shot, Tight turns

title: 2 Foot Stop · Edge Control · Wrist Shot – Backhand
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 31
description: 2 Foot Stop: Set pylons as diagrammed; players leave the side boards with a crossover start, glide on two feet toward a pylon, glide-turn around it and do a two foot stop as they slow down, working both directions. Edge Control: Players follow a pylon or spray-painted path doing exercises such as turning on the outside skate only or the inside skate only, then try it with pucks. Wrist Shot – Backhand: After a demonstration, each player stands still with a puck about 3-4 metres from the boards and shoots backhand at a spot on the boards.
coaching_points: Turn the shoulder first to start the stop.
Practise stops in both directions.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s edge control, two foot stop, wrist shot, Flip shot, Lead pass, Backhand

title: Flip Shot · Puck Dots · Lead Pass
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 31
description: Flip Shot: After a demonstration, each player stands still with a puck about 3-4 metres from the boards and flips it at a spot on the boards. Puck Dots: Lay out pucks as diagrammed; players keep both skates on one side of the pucks and toe drag through the dots. Lead Pass: Set up the course from the diagram; on the signal O2 and O3 skate out with sticks on the ice while O1 and O4 lead them so the puck arrives about five metres out, then O2 carries around the pylon to the O4 line, O1 goes to the O2 line and O3 goes to O1.
coaching_points: Receivers keep the stick on the ice, ready for the pass.
session_objectives: 1. Review: ABC’s edge control, two foot stop, wrist shot, Flip shot, Lead pass, Backhand

title: 2 Foot Stop · Edge Control · Body Fakes
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: 2 Foot Stop: Set pylons as diagrammed; players leave the side boards with a crossover start, glide on two feet toward a pylon, glide-turn around it and do a two foot stop as they slow down, working both directions. Edge Control: Players follow a pylon or spray-painted path, turning on the outside skate only or the inside skate only, then repeat with pucks. Body Fakes: Players line up on the boards and skate at a coach standing halfway across as a defender (or a pylon if short of coaches), using a body fake to get around.
coaching_points: Turn the shoulder first to start the stop.
Practise stops in both directions.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Edge control, two foot stop, puckhandling combinations, Fakes

title: Puckhandling Combinations · Stick Fakes · Flip Shot
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: Puckhandling Combinations: Players skate across the rink working through narrow-wide combination, side-front-side, toe drags, stick through legs, puck through legs and puck in the feet. Stick Fakes: Players line up on the boards and skate at a coach standing halfway across as a defender (or a pylon), using a stick fake to get around. Flip Shot: After a demonstration, each player stands still with a puck about 3-4 metres from the boards and flips it at a spot on the boards.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Edge control, two foot stop, puckhandling combinations, Fakes

title: Pond Hockey (U7 Plan 32)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U7 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: Pond Hockey: Play across the ice in three areas with a puck and pylons for goals. A goal counts only when the puck hits the pylon, and teams need three passes before they can score. There are no goalies. As a variation, try two players sharing one stick.
session_objectives: 1. Review: Edge control, two foot stop, puckhandling combinations, Fakes

title: Practice Rules
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Practice Rules: Coaches introduce themselves and go over the practice rules and guidelines. Make sure players know the signals, what the whistle means and the on-ice safety rules.
coaching_points: Show players each signal you will use.
session_objectives: 1. Practice Rules, Agility, Gliding on one skate, Front V Start, Edge Control

title: Balance and Skating · Chaos · Figure 8’s Inside Edge
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Balance and Skating: From the boards, show the basic stance, then have players go to the far boards and back doing fall-down-and-get-up, one-skate glides, glides with knee bend and gliding arm pumps. Chaos: Players skate around the neutral zone handling a puck. Figure 8's Inside Edge: After a demonstration, players ride the inside edge of the right skate for a full circle, then switch to the left skate to finish the figure 8.
coaching_points: Knees bent, feet shoulder width apart, stick on the ice.
Change directions and vary speed, forward and backward.
Stress good knee bend and upper body control on the edges.
session_objectives: 1. Practice Rules, Agility, Gliding on one skate, Front V Start, Edge Control

title: Shootout · Stationary Stickhandling · Open Ice Carry
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1
description: Shootout: Two lines at the blue line, one player standing with a puck and the other starting on one knee; on the signal the puck carrier attacks the net while the other backchecks, and a backchecker who takes the puck becomes the attacker. Stationary Stickhandling: Check the basic stance, then have players stickhandle a puck in front of them narrow, wide and narrow-wide combination. Open Ice Carry: Players start on the boards and carry the puck across to the other side.
coaching_points: Shift weight as the puck moves across the body.
Practise one-handed carrying on both forehand and backhand.
session_objectives: 1. Practice Rules, Agility, Gliding on one skate, Front V Start, Edge Control

title: Scrimmage – 3 on 3 Cross Ice
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 1, 2, 5, 6, 11, 20
description: Scrimmage – 3 on 3 Cross Ice: Split players into two teams and run two 3 on 3 cross-ice games, one in each end zone. Spare players wait along the blue lines and change on the coach's signal.
coaching_points: Mix in pucks, tennis balls or hockey balls.
Alternate between one, two and three pucks.
session_objectives: 1. Practice Rules, Agility, Gliding on one skate, Front V Start, Edge Control

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 2)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: Warm Up: Divide the ice into four lanes as diagrammed. In each lane players work a different skill: fall down and get up, glide on one skate, jump lines on one and two feet, glide with knee bend, gliding arm pump and C-cuts.
coaching_points: Vary speeds and go both forward and backward.
session_objectives: Balance, Skating, Puckhandling, Front V-Start

title: Chaos · Glide on One Skate · Front V-Start
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: Chaos: Players skate the zone in any direction with a puck, trying moves like narrow-wide combination, toe drag, side-front-side and stickhandling on one leg. Glide on One Skate: Players front V-start, glide on one skate to centre, take 3-4 quick strides and glide to the far boards in a straight line, then use the other skate coming back; do it 4 times, sending the next player when the first reaches the blue line. Front V-Start: On the signal the first player in each group turns the toes out into a V, takes 4-5 running strides to the blue line and stops, then returns to the goal line, doing two foot stops at each line while always facing the same side.
coaching_points: Glide in a straight line.
Always face the same side on the two foot stops.
session_objectives: Balance, Skating, Puckhandling, Front V-Start

title: C-Cuts Around Circle – Inside Foot · Stationary Pairs Passing · Lateral Crossovers – Over Stick
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 2
description: C-Cuts Around Circle – Inside Foot: From the corner, players skate around each circle pushing C-cuts with the inside foot. Stationary Pairs Passing: Partners in the neutral zone pass to each other on forehand and backhand. Lateral Crossovers – Over Stick: Players lay their stick on the ice and step back and forth over it continuously.
coaching_points: Head up, roll the wrists and follow through to the target.
session_objectives: Balance, Skating, Puckhandling, Front V-Start

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 3)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Warm Up: Divide the ice into four lanes as diagrammed. In each lane players do a different skill: glide with knee bend, one-foot glide with the toe on the puck, narrow slalom C-cuts and heel-only C-cuts.
coaching_points: Vary speeds and go both forward and backward.
session_objectives: Agility, Stationary passing and receiving, Pairs passing, Front V-start

title: Chaos · Open Ice Carry · Stationary Passing
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Chaos: Players skate the zone in any direction with a puck, trying narrow-wide combination, toe drag, side-front-side and stickhandling on one leg. Open Ice Carry: Players start on the boards and carry the puck across to the other side. Stationary Passing: Players set up in a box around a circle and pass to anyone; then add a player in the middle who tries to intercept.
coaching_points: Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
Head up, roll the wrists and follow through to the target.
session_objectives: Agility, Stationary passing and receiving, Pairs passing, Front V-start

title: Asteroids · Rabbit/Coyote · Pairs Passing
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Asteroids: Players start on the goal line while coaches line the boards with pucks or tennis balls; on the whistle players skate through the middle while coaches pass or shoot at their skates, and anyone hit moves to the side boards to help until the last player is hit, then repeat with players carrying pucks. Rabbit/Coyote: In pairs, the player with the puck skates anywhere on the whistle while the partner tries to strip it; on the second whistle they rest 30 seconds and switch roles. Pairs Passing: Two lines start in the corner, one on each side of a pylon, and partners skate around the zone passing between the pylons.
coaching_points: Make sure partners take turns passing and receiving on forehand and backhand.
session_objectives: Agility, Stationary passing and receiving, Pairs passing, Front V-start

title: Scrimmage (U9 Plan 3)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 3
description: Scrimmage: Play 4 on 4 with changing rules. Options include three passes before a shot, carrying the puck out of the zone, no sticks (feet only) or adding a second puck.
coaching_points: Change players every 45 seconds to keep the pace high.
session_objectives: Agility, Stationary passing and receiving, Pairs passing, Front V-start

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 4)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Warm Up: Split players into two groups that follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they glide with knee bend, glide on one foot with the toe on the puck, do narrow slalom C-cuts and heel-only C-cuts.
coaching_points: Keep the knees bent.
session_objectives: Forward crossovers, Front V-start, Two-foot stop, Stationary passing

title: Weave · Push and Glide · Forward Crossovers
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Weave: Players weave through pylons on one foot using the inside edge, then one foot using the outside edge, then both feet leading with the front foot, and finally with pucks. Push and Glide: From the boards, players do 3-4 T-pushes across the ice and switch legs coming back, then go backward starting with C-cuts or a backward crossover start and C-cutting to the far boards; repeat 4 times. Forward Crossovers: From the corner, players do forward crossovers around the circles, progressing to backward.
session_objectives: Forward crossovers, Front V-start, Two-foot stop, Stationary passing

title: Front V Start · Stationary Passing · Two Foot Stop
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Front V Start: From the goal line, players front V-start, take 4-5 strides and glide to the blue line, then do the same back; repeat 4-5 times. Stationary Passing: Partners in the neutral zone pass back and forth on forehand and backhand. Two Foot Stop: From the side boards, players front V-start, take 4-5 strides and do a two foot stop, reset to the basic stance and repeat 3-4 times across the ice; do it 4-5 times, stopping both ways, and add a puck if there is time.
coaching_points: Quick feet.
Roll the wrists and follow through.
Come to a complete stop.
session_objectives: Forward crossovers, Front V-start, Two-foot stop, Stationary passing

title: Shootout (U9 Plan 4)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 4
description: Shootout: Two lines at centre ice, using both ends, with one player standing with a puck and the other starting on one knee. On the coach's signal both race to the net; the puck carrier tries to score while the other backchecks. If the backchecker takes the puck, they become the attacker.
coaching_points: The player without the puck starts down on one knee.
Quick feet off the start and protect the puck.
Switch lines after each attempt.
session_objectives: Forward crossovers, Front V-start, Two-foot stop, Stationary passing

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 5)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 5
description: Warm Up: Players skate anywhere on the ice handling a puck. Encourage different moves: narrow-wide combination, side-front-side, toe drag and open ice carry.
coaching_points: Focus on correct technique.
session_objectives: Open Ice Carry, Tight turns, Edge Control, Stationary Passing, Backwards C-cuts

title: Tight Turns / Edge Control · Stationary Passing · Backwards C- Cuts
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 5
description: Tight Turns / Edge Control: From the corner, players skate through pylons making a tight turn around each one, then a full 360 around each on the second pass. Stationary Passing: In a proper puckhandling stance, players pass and receive standing still on forehand and backhand. Backwards C-Cuts: From the side boards in a backward stance, players start with C-cuts or a backward crossover start and C-cut all the way across; repeat 6-7 times and add a puck if there is time.
coaching_points: Knees bent.
Make sure the stance is correct.
Roll the wrists, follow through and cushion the pass.
session_objectives: Open Ice Carry, Tight turns, Edge Control, Stationary Passing, Backwards C-cuts

title: Open Ice Carry · Heel to Heel Glide · Fort Knox
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 5
description: Open Ice Carry: Players carry the puck on the forehand from the goal line to the blue line, stop, and bring it back on the backhand. Heel to Heel Glide: From the boards with a crossover start, players heel-to-heel glide to a pylon, skate around it and repeat coming back. Fort Knox: Two teams start at the hash marks with all pucks piled at centre on the blue line; on the whistle one player from each team skates a 360 around the pylon, grabs a puck and brings it to their corner, then the next teammate goes. When the pucks are gone the team with the most wins; repeat with players skating backward to the corner once they have a puck.
session_objectives: Open Ice Carry, Tight turns, Edge Control, Stationary Passing, Backwards C-cuts

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 6)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 6
description: Warm Up: Players skate clockwise around the ice. Coaches lead skills such as narrow and wide slalom C-cuts, heel-only C-cuts, C-cut crossunders and shoot the duck.
coaching_points: Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, Puckhandling agility, Crossovers, Backwards c-cuts, Tight turns, Bank pass

title: Crossovers 1.6.10/1.6.16 · Backwards C-Cuts / Backwards Stopping · Tight Turns
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 6
description: Crossovers: From the corner, players do crossovers around the circles as diagrammed, both forward and backward. Backwards C-Cuts / Backwards Stopping: From the side boards, players C-cut backward to the far side and finish with a backward one or two foot stop; repeat 4-5 times and add pucks if there is time. Tight Turns: From the corner, players weave the pylons, then do a 360 around each pylon the second time and add pucks the third time.
coaching_points: Full crossover with the outside foot and a strong push with the inside leg.
Start the C-cut with a strong toe push.
Send the next player when the one ahead reaches the hash marks.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, Puckhandling agility, Crossovers, Backwards c-cuts, Tight turns, Bank pass

title: Pairs Passing · British Bulldog · Skill Drill
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 6
description: Pairs Passing: Partners skate counter-clockwise around the ice passing back and forth, alternating forehand and backhand, then progress to pass-and-follow or cross-and-drop; pass only after eye contact with the receiver. British Bulldog: Players start at one end and on the signal try to reach the other end without being caught; caught players join the coaches in the middle as catchers, and it can be played with pucks. Skill Drill: Four groups split between the starting points; in lane 1 the puck carrier goes to the second pylon, reverse pivots and skates backward around the first pylon, then forward to the fourth and repeats, and in lane 2 the carrier banks a pass off the boards to themselves at each pylon.
coaching_points: Make eye contact with the receiver before passing.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, Puckhandling agility, Crossovers, Backwards c-cuts, Tight turns, Bank pass

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 7)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 7
description: Warm Up: Players skate clockwise around the ice. Coaches lead skills such as narrow and wide slalom C-cuts, heel-only C-cuts, C-cut crossunders and shoot the duck.
coaching_points: Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
session_objectives: Front V-Start, Stickhandling, Skating with the Puck, Forwards/Backwards Pivots, Pivots

title: Front V-Start · Stick Handling · Skating with Puck
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 7
description: Front V-Start: From the goal line, players front V-start and stride to the blue line 3-4 times, then add pucks. Stick Handling: Players start stickhandling in place (figure 8s, out to the side, through the legs) and then try the same moves while moving around the area. Skating with Puck: Two groups line up on opposite sides with all the pucks on one side; the carrier skates across, circles their partner, returns and passes across to the partner, who repeats it. Progress to passing to the partner first, circling them, taking the return pass, skating across and passing back.
session_objectives: Front V-Start, Stickhandling, Skating with the Puck, Forwards/Backwards Pivots, Pivots

title: Forward / Backwards Pivots · Skating · C-Cuts – Crossunders
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 7
description: Forward / Backwards Pivots: From the boards on the signal, players skate forward to the top of the circle, pivot to backward to the next circle, pivot again and skate forward to the far boards; after 2-3 reps, start backward. Skating: Players go from the boards to the far boards and back doing stride and bend, stride and jump, heel to heel glide and three quick crossovers. C-Cuts – Crossunders: From the corner around the circles, players push a normal C-cut but bring the drive leg behind the glide foot and push again off the outside edge.
session_objectives: Front V-Start, Stickhandling, Skating with the Puck, Forwards/Backwards Pivots, Pivots

title: Chuck Wagon Races
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 7
description: Chuck Wagon Races: Split players into two groups in opposite corners at opposite ends, with nets moved out to the hash marks. In groups of three, two skaters pull a third, kneeling on the ice, using two sticks along the diagrammed route. Rotate so everyone gets a turn being pulled.
coaching_points: Watch for the criss-cross at centre ice.
session_objectives: Front V-Start, Stickhandling, Skating with the Puck, Forwards/Backwards Pivots, Pivots

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 8)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 8
description: Warm Up: Players skate anywhere on the ice handling a puck. Encourage narrow-wide combination, side-front-side, toe drag, open ice carry and weaving with the puck.
coaching_points: Focus on correct technique.
session_objectives: Tight turns, Lateral Crossovers, Agility, Passing, Forward/Backward pivots, Skating with puck, Backwards C-cuts

title: Tight Turns Acceleration · Lateral Crossovers · Agility Course
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 8
description: Tight Turns Acceleration: From the goal line, players front V-start to a pylon, tight turn around it and accelerate out, then two foot stop back at the goal line; turn both ways, add pucks, and send the next player when the first reaches the pylon. Lateral Crossovers: From the side boards, skate to pylon 1 and two foot stop, lateral crossovers to pylon 2, skate forward and lateral crossovers to pylon 3, right-leg C-cuts to pylon 4, lateral crossovers to pylon 5 and left-leg C-cuts back to the start; run it in reverse the second time and add pucks. Agility Course: From the corner, crossovers around the circle, skate to the pylon at the top of the far circle, pivot and skate backward to the goal line, two foot stop and return; start backward the second time, use pucks the third, then switch sides.
coaching_points: Accelerate hard out of the turn.
session_objectives: Tight turns, Lateral Crossovers, Agility, Passing, Forward/Backward pivots, Skating with puck, Backwards C-cuts

title: 5 Player Passing · Pivots · Skating with Puck
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 8
description: 5 Player Passing: The puck moves 5 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 1, 1 to 4 and 4 to 5, then repeats, using forehand and backhand passes and rotating positions. Pivots: From the side boards, skate backward to centre, pivot forward to the far boards and two foot stop; then skate forward to centre, pivot backward to the boards and do a backward two foot stop; repeat with pucks. Skating with Puck: Players stickhandle from the side boards to the far side, then push the puck on the forehand the second time and on the backhand the third time, progressing to dropping the puck into the skates and kicking it back up to the stick.
session_objectives: Tight turns, Lateral Crossovers, Agility, Passing, Forward/Backward pivots, Skating with puck, Backwards C-cuts

title: Shootout (U9 Plan 8)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 8
description: Shootout: Two lines at centre ice, using both ends, with one player standing with a puck and the other starting on one knee. On the coach's signal both race to the net; the puck carrier tries to score while the other backchecks. If the backchecker takes the puck, they become the attacker.
coaching_points: The player without the puck starts down on one knee.
Quick feet off the start and protect the puck.
Switch lines after each attempt.
session_objectives: Tight turns, Lateral Crossovers, Agility, Passing, Forward/Backward pivots, Skating with puck, Backwards C-cuts

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 9)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 9
description: Warm Up: Players skate counter-clockwise around the ice. On the whistle each player makes a tight turn toward the boards and accelerates out of it. After a couple of minutes, add pucks.
coaching_points: Change direction on the whistle, sometimes with two whistles back to back.
Have players skate in both directions.
session_objectives: Tight Turns, Stopping with puck, Stickhandling, Open ice carry, backwards striding, moving to space, stationary shooting

title: Backwards Striding · Moving to Space · Stationary Shooting
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 9
description: Backwards Striding: Players skate backward across the ice and finish with a backward two foot stop at the boards; as a variation, one partner starts on the side boards skating forward while the other starts halfway across skating backward, racing to reach the far boards first. Moving to Space: Groups of four stand on painted spots in a square; 1 and 2 pass to 3 and 4, then 1 and 2 swap spots and get passes back from 3 and 4, then 3 and 4 swap and receive, using forehand and backhand. Stationary Shooting: In pairs with 4-5 pucks, the passer on the boards feeds a shooter four metres out; after 5-6 shots switch roles, then repeat with a backhand sweep shot.
coaching_points: Pass and receive on both forehand and backhand.
session_objectives: Tight Turns, Stopping with puck, Stickhandling, Open ice carry, backwards striding, moving to space, stationary shooting

title: Stopping with the Puck · Rabbit / Coyote · Body and Head Fakes
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 9
description: Stopping with the Puck: On the whistle, players accelerate with the puck to centre and two foot stop, then accelerate to the far boards and stop again, always facing the same side, while using narrow-wide combination, side-front-side and open ice carry. Rabbit / Coyote: In pairs, the player with the puck skates anywhere on the whistle while the partner tries to take it; on the second whistle rest 30 seconds and switch roles. Body and Head Fakes: Players carry a puck from the boards doing a 360 around each pylon to the far boards, then use body and head fakes around the pylons coming back.
coaching_points: Always stop facing the same side.
session_objectives: Tight Turns, Stopping with puck, Stickhandling, Open ice carry, backwards striding, moving to space, stationary shooting

title: Half Ice Scrimmage
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 9
description: Half Ice Scrimmage: Split players into four teams and run two half-ice games. Spare players wait on the benches. The number of whistles tells each team how many players go on.
coaching_points: Mix in pucks, tennis balls or hockey balls.
Alternate between one, two and three pucks.
session_objectives: Tight Turns, Stopping with puck, Stickhandling, Open ice carry, backwards striding, moving to space, stationary shooting

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 10)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 10
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, slalom, C-cut crossunders, three quick crossovers, stops and starts, stride and bend, and jump strides.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, balance and agility, stationary shooting, backwards striding, lateral crossovers

title: Rabbit / Coyote · Agility Skate · Short Pass – Long Pass
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 10
description: Rabbit / Coyote: In pairs, the player with the puck skates anywhere on the whistle while the partner tries to take it; on the second whistle rest 30 seconds and switch roles. Agility Skate: From the boards at the blue line, players skate backward to the far blue line and two foot stop, lateral crossover along the blue line to the far boards, skate forward toward the blue line and two foot stop again, then go to the back of the line. Short Pass – Long Pass: Partners share one puck and start close; on the signal the carrier makes a short pass and skates to open ice for a long pass, then follows it so they are close again, alternating so both make short and long passes.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, balance and agility, stationary shooting, backwards striding, lateral crossovers

title: Pairs Passing · Stationary Shooting · (backwards Striding)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 10
description: Pairs Passing: Partners pass back and forth between the pylons around the zone, trying one-touch passes the second time through and using forehand and backhand. Stationary Shooting: Groups of three take a spot on the boards with 5-6 pucks; 1 passes to 2, 2 passes to 3 and 3 shoots forehand or backhand, then 3 moves to 1, 1 to 2 and 2 becomes the shooter. Backwards Striding: One partner starts on the side boards skating forward while the other starts halfway across skating backward, racing to the far boards; after a few reps the forward skater carries a puck.
coaching_points: Use both forehand and backhand when passing.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, balance and agility, stationary shooting, backwards striding, lateral crossovers

title: 1-2-3 on 0 – Relay Race (U9 Plan 10)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 10
description: 1-2-3 on 0 – Relay Race: Move the nets to the goal line below the faceoff dots at each end. Players line up in even groups outside the blue line, each with a puck. The first player attacks and keeps shooting until scoring, then skates back outside the blue line and the next player joins for a 2 on 0, then 3 on 0 and so on.
coaching_points: Use four nets if needed.
Every player must touch the puck once before the shot.
When the last player scores, everyone dives across the blue line.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, balance and agility, stationary shooting, backwards striding, lateral crossovers

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 11)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 11
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, slalom, C-cut crossunders, three quick crossovers, stops and starts, stride and bend, and jump strides. Add pucks if you like.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Bank pass, pairs passing, agility skating, backwards crossover start, pass and follow, shooting

title: Backwards Cross-Over Start – Agility Movement · Pairs Passing – Pass and Follow · Shooting
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 11
description: Backwards Cross-Over Start – Agility Movement: Players backward crossover start to the first blue line, lateral crossover to the pylon, backward crossover start to the hash marks, pivot and skate forward to the goal line, lateral crossover, skate backward to the blue line and lateral crossover to the boards, then backward crossover start, pivot at the hash marks and skate forward. Pairs Passing – Pass and Follow: Partners pass while crossing the ice and swap positions, with the receiver moving in front and the passer going behind; go slowly at first. Shooting: Players form a semi-circle in front of the net and coaches pass randomly for shots, alternating standing shots, shots after a few strides and dekes; players can take over passing.
coaching_points: Go slowly the first few times through the pass and follow.
session_objectives: Bank pass, pairs passing, agility skating, backwards crossover start, pass and follow, shooting

title: Bank Pass · Pairs Passing · Shootout
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 11
description: Bank Pass: Everyone starts in one corner with a puck, skates down one side banking a pass off the boards at each pylon (set about one metre from the boards), then weaves back through the pylons to the start; repeat 4-5 times. Pairs Passing: Partners skate around the zone passing back and forth, alternating forehand and backhand, progressing to pass-and-follow or cross-and-drop, and passing only after eye contact. Shootout: Two lines at centre ice using both ends, one player standing with a puck and one on a knee; on the signal the carrier attacks the net while the other backchecks, and a backchecker who takes the puck becomes the attacker.
coaching_points: Make eye contact with the receiver before passing.
session_objectives: Bank pass, pairs passing, agility skating, backwards crossover start, pass and follow, shooting

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 12)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 12
description: Warm Up: Players form five groups at one end and pair up, each partner holding opposite ends of two sticks. One partner pulls while the other resists by braking with one skate, and they switch at the far end to come back. Add slalom and C-cuts while pulling, then repeat skating backward.
coaching_points: Keep the tempo high.
Run it in waves.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, support passing, balance and agility, pass and move, stationary passing, stationary shooting

title: Backward Crossovers – Reaching · Pairs Passing · Short Pass – Long Pass
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 12
description: Backward Crossovers – Reaching: From the corner, players do backward crossovers around each circle, reaching the inside foot out as far as they can. Pairs Passing: Partners skate around the zone passing back and forth, alternating forehand and backhand, progressing to pass-and-follow or cross-and-drop, and passing only after eye contact. Short Pass – Long Pass: Partners share one puck and start close; the carrier makes a short pass and skates to open ice for a long pass, then follows it to get close again, alternating so both make short and long passes.
coaching_points: Reach the inside foot out as far as possible.
Make eye contact with the receiver before passing.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, support passing, balance and agility, pass and move, stationary passing, stationary shooting

title: Pass and Move · Stationary Passing · Stationary Shooting
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 12
description: Pass and Move: 1 banks a pass behind the net to 2, weaves through the pylons as diagrammed and heads to the net, takes a pass from 2 and shoots, then goes to the end of the other line while 2 makes the next bank pass. Stationary Passing: Partners pass on forehand and backhand, gradually moving farther apart and alternating receiving on the forehand and passing on the backhand and vice versa. Stationary Shooting: Players spread around the zone practising wrist and backhand shots, and can shoot on a goalie.
coaching_points: Demonstrate the first time through.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, support passing, balance and agility, pass and move, stationary passing, stationary shooting

title: Chuckwagon Races
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 12
description: Chuckwagon Races: Split players into two groups in opposite corners at opposite ends, with nets moved out to the hash marks. In groups of three, two skaters pull a third, kneeling on the ice, using two sticks along the diagrammed route. Rotate so everyone gets a turn being pulled.
coaching_points: Watch for the criss-cross at centre ice.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, support passing, balance and agility, pass and move, stationary passing, stationary shooting

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 13)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 13
