description: Warm Up: Everyone stickhandles a puck in the neutral zone and tries to knock pucks off other players' sticks. A puck that leaves through the blue lines into an end zone is out. Players who lose their puck keep trying to knock out the others' pucks until the last puck is gone.
coaching_points: Keep heads up.
Players must keep skating.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, tight turn puck control, telescope passing, pass and shoot, two foot stop, crossover start, flip pass, fakes

title: Tight Turn Puck Control · Telescoping Passing · Relay Race
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 13
description: Tight Turn Puck Control: From the corner, players weave the pylons with a puck and finish with a shot; the second time, they send the puck past one side of each pylon, skate around the other side and pick it up. Telescoping Passing: Partners work up the ice with one skating forward with the puck and the other skating backward to take the pass, then stopping and going forward, while the passer stops and skates backward to receive. Relay Race: Two groups start in the corners while the coach places a puck at centre; on the signal players weave the pylons and race for it, and the first one there attacks the net while the other tries to stop the shot.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, tight turn puck control, telescope passing, pass and shoot, two foot stop, crossover start, flip pass, fakes

title: Pass and Shoot · 2 Foot Stop / Crossover Start · Flip Pass
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 13
description: Pass and Shoot: Player A in the corner passes to 1, who shoots, then to 2, who shoots; Player B then does the same, and 1 and 2 move to the ends of the other lines. 2 Foot Stop / Crossover Start: From the side boards, players use a front crossover start, two foot stop at the far side and come back the same way, 3-4 times each. Flip Pass: Partners take a spot on the boards with a stick laid between them; 2 flips 5-6 pucks over it to 1, who takes one on the forehand, turns 180 and shoots backhand, then takes the next on the backhand, turns and shoots forehand.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, tight turn puck control, telescope passing, pass and shoot, two foot stop, crossover start, flip pass, fakes

title: 1 on 1 Deking
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 13
description: 1 on 1 Deking: Partners pair off, one on the boards with a puck and one at mid ice facing them with the stick on the ice. The puck carrier skates out and pulls the puck under the defender's stick from left to right, then skates to the other side. Do it four times, then pull from right to left, and switch roles.
coaching_points: The defender stays passive.
session_objectives: Pairs passing, tight turn puck control, telescope passing, pass and shoot, two foot stop, crossover start, flip pass, fakes

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 14)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 14
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, slalom, C-cut crossunders, three quick crossovers, stops and starts, stride and bend, and jump strides.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Agility Skating, Pass and Shoot, Fakes, Flip pass and move, Backwards stopping, pivots.

title: Pass and Shoot · Faking · Flip Pass and Move
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 14
description: Pass and Shoot: A player in the corner passes to a teammate at the top of the circle and drives to the net, while a player from the other side moves into the slot, takes the pass and shoots, with the first player crashing for the rebound; lines rotate clockwise. Faking: On one side of the red line, slide the puck between pylons and under the sticks resting on them, picking it up on the far side on forehand and backhand, then weave the cones set on the other side. Flip Pass and Move: With a stick on the ice between them, 1 flips to 2, 2 passes to 4 and 4 to 3, while 1 skates behind the net, curls around the pylon, takes a pass from 3 and wrist shoots; rotate 2 to 1 to 4 to 3 to 2.
session_objectives: Agility Skating, Pass and Shoot, Fakes, Flip pass and move, Backwards stopping, pivots.

title: Backwards Stopping · Pivots · Chaos
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 14
description: Backwards Stopping: From the boards, players do a backward crossover start to centre and two foot stop, then repeat to the far boards, adding pucks if wanted. Pivots: From the boards, players take 5-6 forward strides, pivot, take 5-6 backward strides, aiming for three pivots before the far boards. Chaos: Players skate the zone randomly and stop with the puck under control on the signal, then go again on the next whistle, stickhandling narrow-wide, side-front-side, on one leg, hands together and hands wide.
coaching_points: Everyone goes at once.
Encourage quick feet.
Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
session_objectives: Agility Skating, Pass and Shoot, Fakes, Flip pass and move, Backwards stopping, pivots.

title: 1-2-3 on 0 – Relay Race (U9 Plan 14)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 14
description: 1-2-3 on 0 – Relay Race: Move the nets to the goal line below the faceoff dots at each end. Players line up in even groups outside the blue line, each with a puck. The first player attacks and keeps shooting until scoring, then skates back outside the blue line and the next player joins for a 2 on 0, then 3 on 0 and so on.
coaching_points: Split into teams and keep score.
Teams switch roles after three outs.
session_objectives: Agility Skating, Pass and Shoot, Fakes, Flip pass and move, Backwards stopping, pivots.

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 15)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 15
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, backward slalom, C-cut crossunders, shoot the duck, stops and starts, and stride and bend and jump strides both forward and backward.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Backwards lateral crossovers, pass and move, pass and follow, shooting while moving

title: Pass and Move · Pass and Follow · Relay Race
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 15
description: Pass and Move: 1 passes to D1, D1 moves it to D2 while 1 swings around the defenceman, takes a pass from D2 and shoots, then joins the line in the opposite corner while 2 starts by passing to D2; the D use both forehand and backhand. Pass and Follow: 1 carries the puck and swaps positions with 2 by crossing in front, passes to 2 and they swap again with 2 in front, then at the far side both tight turn around the pylons and return to the opposite line. Relay Race: Two groups start in the corners while the coach places a puck at centre; on the signal players weave the pylons and race for it, and the winner attacks the net while the other defends.
coaching_points: Defencemen pass on both forehand and backhand.
session_objectives: Backwards lateral crossovers, pass and move, pass and follow, shooting while moving

title: Chaos · Backwards Lateral Crossovers · Shooting While Moving
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 15
description: Chaos: Players skate anywhere with a puck trying moves such as on one leg, hands together, hands wide, toe drag and rotation. Backwards Lateral Crossovers: From the goal line, players skate backward the length of the ice doing two lateral crossovers left then two right, for three lengths, then repeat with three each way. Shooting While Moving: Players spread out practising wrist and backhand shots, can shoot on a goalie, and then skate toward the boards and shoot on the move.
coaching_points: Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
Encourage quick feet and full crossovers.
Players must be moving when they release the puck.
session_objectives: Backwards lateral crossovers, pass and move, pass and follow, shooting while moving

title: Baseball (U9)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 15
description: Baseball: Split into two groups, one in each end, with two teams per end and two pylons near the blue line. Five fielders spread out in the slot. On the whistle the player in the corner passes to a fielder and tries to skate around the pylons and back to the end of the line. All five fielders must touch the puck before shooting, and if they score before the skater gets back, the skater is out.
coaching_points: Split into teams and keep score.
Teams switch roles after three outs.
session_objectives: Backwards lateral crossovers, pass and move, pass and follow, shooting while moving

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 16)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 16
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, backward slalom, C-cut crossunders, shoot the duck, stops and starts, and stride and bend and jump strides both forward and backward. Add pucks if you like.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: bank pass, agility skate, crossovers, mirroring, pass and move

title: Crossovers · Mirror Drill · Bank Pass
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 16
description: Crossovers: From one corner, players do forward crossovers around the first circle two and a half times, pivot to backward heading to the second circle, and do backward crossovers around it two and a half times. Mirror Drill: Partners line up on the boards as diagrammed; one skates backward weaving left to right to left while the other skates forward using lateral crossovers to mirror them, then they switch on the way back and repeat with pucks. Bank Pass: Everyone starts on the boards with a puck, weaves through the pylons across the ice and comes back banking a pass off the boards at each pylon.
session_objectives: bank pass, agility skate, crossovers, mirroring, pass and move

title: Pass and Move · Chaos · Pass and Move
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 16
description: Pass and Move: 1 and 2 exchange passes, swing before the blue line and come back toward the net, where 1 passes to 2 for a shot; players return to opposite corners. Chaos: Players skate anywhere with a puck trying moves like one leg, hands together, hands wide, toe drag, rotation and side to side behind the body. Pass and Move: 1 passes to 2 and skates around the pylons, 2 passes to 3, who carries behind the net and out toward the blue line and passes to 1 for a shot; rotate 1 to 3, 3 to 2 and 2 to 1.
coaching_points: Pass only after eye contact.
Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
Talk about why timing matters.
session_objectives: bank pass, agility skate, crossovers, mirroring, pass and move

title: Scrimmage – Full Ice
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 16, 17, 18
description: Scrimmage – Full Ice: Split players into two teams and play 4 on 4. Players change on the whistle.
coaching_points: Mix in pucks, tennis balls or hockey balls.
Alternate between one, two and three pucks.
session_objectives: bank pass, agility skate, crossovers, mirroring, pass and move

title: Barteaux Set-Up (U9 Plan 17)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 17
description: Barteaux Set-Up: Players run the circuit twice from each side. On the circles, start with forward C-cuts and progress to forward crossovers; down the sides, alternate left and right leg C-cuts; through the middle cones, tight turn around each cone and progress to long, exaggerated crossovers. When everyone is done, run it back in the opposite direction, using pucks the third and fourth times.
coaching_points: Start players in one corner and send them one after another.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and Follow, Intro to Angling

title: Short Pass – Long Pass · British Bulldog · Angling
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 17
description: Short Pass – Long Pass: Partners share a puck; 1 makes a short pass to 2 and stretches out as a long-pass option, then after the long pass moves in tight to support for a short one, alternating continuously. British Bulldog: Players start on the boards and on the signal try to reach the other side without being caught, with caught players joining the coaches in the middle; can be done with pucks. Angling: For balance, the coach pushes the chest of a player standing tall with feet together, then again in a low staggered stance to show it is stable; for stability, partners lock elbows and push toward the boards, introducing protecting the middle, then without locking elbows keep the partner on the boards side, both directions. To angle a puck carrier starting near the boards, both face the same way while the defender keeps the attacker on the boards side and attacks the stick where blade meets shaft moving up ice, first without and then with a puck.
coaching_points: Low stance with bent ankles and knees and staggered feet gives stability.
Protect the middle, the high-scoring part of the ice.
Attack the stick where the blade meets the shaft.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and Follow, Intro to Angling

title: Give and Go · Pass Behind – Pull Puck Through Legs · Chaos
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 17
description: Give and Go: A player carries out of the corner, makes a short pass to a coach and moves to open ice for the return, does the same with a second coach, then drives the net for a shot. Pass Behind – Pull Puck Through Legs: Partners face the same direction; 1 passes to 2, who reaches the blade behind the body and pulls the puck through the legs. Chaos: Players skate anywhere with a puck trying stick through legs, puck through legs from behind, switching hands and 360 spins.
coaching_points: Send the next player when the first takes the first pass from the coach.
Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and Follow, Intro to Angling

title: Barteaux Set-Up (U9 Plan 18)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 18
description: Barteaux Set-Up: Players run the circuit twice from each side. On the circles, review forward C-cuts, progress to forward crossovers and introduce backward C-cuts. Down the sides, alternate left and right leg C-cuts, switching to long strides halfway. Through the middle cones, pick up a puck off the circle and handle it back through the cones for a shot.
coaching_points: Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and follow, Stationary Stick Checking, Angling, Moving Puck Control, Deflections

title: Short Pass – Long Pass · Stationary Stick Checking · Angling
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 18
description: Short Pass – Long Pass: Partners share a puck; 1 makes a short pass to 2 and stretches out as a long-pass option, then after the long pass moves in tight to support for a short one, alternating continuously. Stationary Stick Checking: After demonstrating the press and the lift, partners stand side by side; on the whistle 1 stickhandles in place and on the second whistle 2 traps or lifts the stick. Angling: After coaches demonstrate control skating, mirroring and the hip pocket, pair players of similar skating ability; 1 skates along the boards with quick starts, stops and direction changes while 2 control skates and mirrors, keeping 1 outside in the bad ice, going all the way around the ice a couple of times before switching direction.
coaching_points: Keep the puck carrier to the outside, in the bad ice.
Pair players of similar skating ability.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and follow, Stationary Stick Checking, Angling, Moving Puck Control, Deflections

title: Follow Your Pass · Puck Control · Deflections
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 18
description: Follow Your Pass: Player 1 leaves the corner with a puck, passes at centre to a player on the diagonal line and follows the pass, and each receiver moves quickly across to make the next pass, finishing by driving the net and tapping the post. Puck Control: From the boards, players weave pylons with the puck on the forehand only, forehand one-handed, puck inside the pylon off the stick, and puck inside the pylon on the stick. Deflections: Set players as diagrammed; the shooter takes a pass from each corner and shoots along the ice for the net-front player to tip, working low and high deflections.
coaching_points: Keep the tempo high and players moving.
Demonstrate before starting.
Quick feet and drive the net with the puck.
session_objectives: Give and Go, Pass and follow, Stationary Stick Checking, Angling, Moving Puck Control, Deflections

title: Barteaux Set-Up (U9 Plan 19)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 19
description: Barteaux Set-Up: Players run the circuit twice from each side. On the circles, review backward C-cuts and progress to backward crossovers. Down the sides, do backward C-cuts alternating legs and backward striding. Through the middle cones, tight turn and skate backward around the cones, using pucks the third and fourth times.
coaching_points: Players should know the circuit and use correct technique.
session_objectives: Agility, Quick Feet, Creative Stickhandling, Deflections

title: Mario Moves · 4 Step Quick Feet
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 19
description: Mario Moves: Partners face each other all the way down the ice; 1 skates at 2 and makes a move, goes around, tight turns back to position, and 2 does the same. Spend about two minutes on each move in order: head fake forehand, head fake backhand, head fake and slide the puck through the skates to pick up forehand, then backhand, head fake and attack the triangle of stick and skates forehand and backhand, and drive around an active stick. 4 Step Quick Feet: In their own space in the neutral zone, players step over a stick laid on the ice touching a hand down each side; then skate forward over the stick touching down at each end with tight turns; then pivot forward to backward at each end of the stick; finally partners stand facing each other with sticks upright on the knob and on the whistle let go and V-start to catch the other's stick before it falls.
coaching_points: Let players be creative with their moves.
Demonstrate all four steps so players can see them.
Good skating position, head up and balanced.
session_objectives: Agility, Quick Feet, Creative Stickhandling, Deflections

title: 1-2-3 on -0 Relay · Puck Control · Passing
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 19
description: 1-2-3 on 0 Relay: Move the nets to the goal line below the faceoff dots, with players in even groups inside the blue line, each with a puck; the first player shoots until scoring, skates back outside the blue line and the next joins for 2 on 0, then 3 on 0, and when the last player scores everyone dives across the blue line. Puck Control: From the boards in the neutral zone, players skate into the pylon box making a move on each pylon in random order, then straddle the puck dots and stickhandle through them. Passing: At the far end, players do the one-touch passing circle.
coaching_points: Every player must touch the puck once before the shot.
Let players be creative with their moves.
session_objectives: Agility, Quick Feet, Creative Stickhandling, Deflections

title: Shootout (U9 Plan 19)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 19
description: Shootout: Two lines at centre ice, using both ends, with one player standing with a puck and the other starting on one knee. On the coach's signal both race to the net; the puck carrier tries to score while the other backchecks. If the backchecker takes the puck, they become the attacker.
coaching_points: The player without the puck starts down on one knee.
Quick feet off the start.
session_objectives: Agility, Quick Feet, Creative Stickhandling, Deflections

title: Barteaux Set-Up (U9 Plan 20)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 20
description: Barteaux Set-Up: Each player runs the circuit twice from each side. On the circles, review forward crossovers and progress to crossunders, holding the inside edge of the crossing skate while the back skate pumps to keep speed. Down the sides, take long strides focusing on posture, power and full recovery to the middle. Through the middle cones, hold the inside edge of the outside foot around each cone, adding pucks the third and fourth times.
coaching_points: Give corrective feedback.
Focus on posture, power and full recovery on long strides.
session_objectives: Agility, Give and go, Net Drive, - outside/inside/delay, Shooting in motion

title: Outside In, Inside Out, Drive, Delay - Part I · 4 Step Quick Feet · Outside In, Inside Out, Drive, Delay - Part Ii
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 20
description: Outside In, Inside Out, Drive, Delay - Part I: Introduce attacking the net; first players drive to centre, pick up a puck and curl outside toward the boards to drive wide and shoot in stride, then they go inside, drive down the wall, delay to find an opening and drive the net. 4 Step Quick Feet: In their own space, players step over a stick on the ice touching a hand down each side, then skate forward over the stick touching down at each end with tight turns, then pivot forward to backward at each end, and finally release an upright stick on the whistle and V-start to catch the partner's stick before it falls. Outside In, Inside Out, Drive, Delay - Part II: Players drive up the boards, pick up a puck at centre and drive the middle lane for a shot in stride, then repeat the first pattern with a coach as passive pressure.
coaching_points: Players accelerate after picking up the puck.
Give each player feedback.
session_objectives: Agility, Give and go, Net Drive, - outside/inside/delay, Shooting in motion

title: Asteroids · Shooting in Motion · Chaos
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 20
description: Asteroids: Players line up on the boards and on the whistle skate to the other end while coaches on the blue line or goal line shoot pucks and tennis balls at their skates; anyone hit joins the coaches until one player is left, and it can be run with players carrying pucks. Shooting in Motion: Players spread out practising wrist and backhand shots, then skate toward the boards and shoot on the move. Chaos: Players skate anywhere with a puck trying stick through legs, puck through legs from behind, switching hands and 360 spins.
coaching_points: Keep the puck down.
Players must be moving when they release the puck.
Change direction and vary speed, forward and backward.
session_objectives: Agility, Give and go, Net Drive, - outside/inside/delay, Shooting in motion

title: Moe Mania 1.6.21
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 21
description: Moe Mania: Set players up as diagrammed and spray paint a line halfway between each pair of cones to mark where to pivot. Players skate forward toward the first cone and pivot to backward at the paint line, repeating through the whole course. They always pivot so they keep their eyes on the cone ahead, leading with the stick for balance. Run the whole session without pucks.
coaching_points: Focus on correct technique.
Pivot so eye contact stays on the cone ahead.
Lead with the stick to stay balanced on the pivot.
session_objectives: Angling, Gap Mirroring, Intro to 1 on 1

title: Angling · Gap Mirroring · Angling
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 21
description: Angling: Demonstrate taking an inside-out angle to a puck in the corner with head up and a shoulder check; the coach dumps a puck in, the player retrieves it on a good angle and drives around the circle for a shot. Gap Mirroring: As an introduction to gap control, partners face each other and the follower mirrors every forward, backward, sideways move or stop of the leader, staying within two stick lengths for 40 seconds, then rests and switches roles. Angling: As a progression, a second player follows the first in applying passive pressure, so the puck carrier must take a good angle and drive around the circle to the net while the chaser works on angling position and controlled skating.
coaching_points: Take the puck inside out with head up and a shoulder check.
Stay within two stick lengths when mirroring.
session_objectives: Angling, Gap Mirroring, Intro to 1 on 1

title: Chaos · Pass Behind – Off Skate to Stick · Intro to 1 on 1
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 21
description: Chaos: Three players at a time leave the corner and handle pucks between the circles, then on the whistle tight turn and attack the net for a shot while a new group of three starts from the opposite corner. Pass Behind – Off Skate to Stick: Partners face the same direction; 1 passes to 2, who takes it off the skate and directs it to the stick. Intro to 1 on 1: Explain good ice (middle of the rink, good shooting and scoring spots) and bad ice (outside, with the defender between the attacker and the net); from one corner at a time, the puck carrier goes around the cone inside out toward the bad ice while the defender skates outside in to take away the middle.
coaching_points: Head up, tight turns, quick feet and protect the puck.
Defenders take away the middle, good ice.
session_objectives: Angling, Gap Mirroring, Intro to 1 on 1

title: Scrimmage (U9 Plan 21)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 21, 32
description: Scrimmage: Split into two teams for a full-ice scrimmage. Change the rules to keep it interesting: three passes before a shot, a pass across each line, no sticks and skates only, or no sticks and pushing the puck with gloves.
coaching_points: Use two or three pucks, tennis balls and so on.
session_objectives: Angling, Gap Mirroring, Intro to 1 on 1

title: Moe Mania (U9 Plan 22)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 22
description: Moe Mania: Set players up as diagrammed and spray paint a line halfway between each pair of cones to mark where to pivot. Players skate forward toward the first cone and pivot to backward at the paint line, repeating through the whole course. They always pivot so they keep their eyes on the cone ahead, leading with the stick for balance. Start without pucks and add them once players are ready.
coaching_points: Focus on correct technique.
Pivot so eye contact stays on the cone ahead.
Lead with the stick to stay balanced on the pivot.
session_objectives: Passing and Moving, One Man Drive, Two Man Drive, Puck support

title: Pass and Move · Support Passing · Pig in the Middle
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 22
description: Pass and Move: The puck goes O1 to O2 to O3 to O4 while O1 follows the pass, curls between O2 and O3, takes a pass from O4 and shoots. Support Passing: Three players work inside a four-pylon box; the puck stays with the middle player and the others move so the carrier always has two options without passing through the box. Pig in the Middle: In groups of four, three pass the puck around while the fourth tries to intercept, and whoever turns it over goes to the middle.
coaching_points: Pass hard.
Keep the stick on the ice as a target.
session_objectives: Passing and Moving, One Man Drive, Two Man Drive, Puck support

title: Two Man Drive · Wrist Shot · One Man Drive
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 22
description: Two Man Drive: Building toward the attack triangle, the coach holds the puck in the middle; a winger from the left boards takes a pass in stride and drives hard to the net while a middle player drives the middle lane but control skates to stay a high option, and the winger either shoots and chases the rebound or drops it to the middle and drives the net for a tip, screen or rebound. Wrist Shot: Players spread out practising wrist and backhand shots, aiming high but under the glass. One Man Drive: A player from the left boards takes the coach's pass in stride, drives the net, shoots from the circle and attacks the rebound; then a centre player takes a pass and drives straight down the middle, followed by a player off the other boards, running from both ends with spray-painted circles marking where to drive for rebounds.
coaching_points: Players pay attention and are ready to go.
Follow through on the shot.
Keep the drill flowing so players stay moving.
session_objectives: Passing and Moving, One Man Drive, Two Man Drive, Puck support

title: 1-2-3 on O Relay
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 22
description: 1-2-3 on O Relay: On the whistle three players attack the net using the three man drive and play until they score, then come out for another puck. On the second attack a player who has not scored must score, and on the third the last player who has not scored must score. Run from both ends; the first team with all three scorers wins and the other team does a fun penalty such as skating, push ups or jumping jacks.
session_objectives: Passing and Moving, One Man Drive, Two Man Drive, Puck support

title: Moe Mania (U9 Plan 23)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 23
description: Moe Mania: Set players up as diagrammed and spray paint a line halfway between each pair of cones to mark where to pivot. Players skate forward toward the first cone and pivot to backward at the paint line, repeating through the whole course. They always pivot so they keep their eyes on the cone ahead, leading with the stick for balance. Use pucks from the start in this session.
coaching_points: Focus on correct technique.
Pivot so eye contact stays on the cone ahead.
Lead with the stick to stay balanced on the pivot.
session_objectives: Open Ice Angling, Intro to breakouts, Wrist shot, 3 man drives

title: Facing Goal · Facing Inside Shoulder · Facing Goal and Pivot
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 23
description: Facing Goal: Partners both face the goal; the defender takes inside position, pushes the attacker toward the boards, attacks the stick where blade meets shaft and squeezes the attacker out to win the puck. Facing Inside Shoulder: The attacker faces the far boards and the defender faces the attacker, lining up their helmet with the attacker's inside shoulder and skating backward to force them outside. Facing Goal and Pivot: Partners both face the goal; the defender takes inside position skating forward, then pivots to backward while still forcing the attacker toward the boards.
coaching_points: Take inside position and force the attacker to the boards.
Attack the stick where the blade meets the shaft.
session_objectives: Open Ice Angling, Intro to breakouts, Wrist shot, 3 man drives

title: Breakout Introduction · Wrist Shot · 3 Man Drive
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 23
description: Breakout Introduction: Explain a basic breakout option, put players in the diagrammed formation and run it to each side, rotating everyone through every position. Wrist Shot: Players spread out practising wrist and backhand shots, aiming high but under the glass. 3 Man Drive: Building on the two man drive, the coach in the middle passes to either winger in stride; the puck carrier drives the net, the middle player drives the middle lane but control skates as a high option, and the far winger drives the far post, while the carrier chooses to shoot and chase the rebound, drop to the middle and drive for a tip, screen or rebound, or pass across to the far winger.
coaching_points: Rotate players through all positions.
session_objectives: Open Ice Angling, Intro to breakouts, Wrist shot, 3 man drives

title: British Bulldog (U9)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 23
description: British Bulldog: Players line up at one end and on the coach's signal try to reach the other end without being caught. Caught players go to centre and help the coaches catch others. It can also be played with pucks.
coaching_points: Remind catchers of the angling tips from earlier drills.
session_objectives: Open Ice Angling, Intro to breakouts, Wrist shot, 3 man drives

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 24)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 24
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner and follow the diagrammed path. Along the way they do forward and backward scissor skating, slalom, C-cut crossunders, three quick crossovers, stops and starts, stride and bend, and jump strides.
coaching_points: Coaches lead and demonstrate each activity.
Players go one after another.
session_objectives: Fun day, Fun games incorporating skill combinations

title: 2 on 0 Down Low · Sweeping Sticks · Relay 2 on 2
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 24
description: 2 on 0 Down Low: Nets sit on the goal line with a goalie in each; on the whistle two players from each team attack their diagonal net 2 on 0, and a team that scores can go after the other team's puck and score on its original net, playing until both pucks are in. Sweeping Sticks: One partner kneels with the stick flat on the ice and sweeps it back and forth through 180 degrees on the whistle while the other, in a good stance, handles a puck and pulls it in to the body to avoid the stick; switch after 40 seconds. Relay 2 on 2: Two teams race against each other, with the first player in each line skating a set pattern (changing each time, possibly around pylons) to a puck the coach places; more players can go at once for 3 on 3 or 4 on 4.
coaching_points: Keep a good hockey stance and pull the puck in close.
session_objectives: Fun day, Fun games incorporating skill combinations

title: Cross Ice Support · Moving Puck Control · Stick Relay
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 24
description: Cross Ice Support: Players line up on the goal line and blue line as diagrammed; on the whistle three from each team play 3 on 3, but each team must pass to a teammate on the line before scoring, and the next threes come on at the next whistle. Moving Puck Control: From the boards, players weave pylons with the puck on the forehand only, forehand one-handed, puck inside the pylon off the stick and on the stick, then on the way back do narrow and wide slalom with toe drags. Stick Relay: Two teams split their players between the two ends; the first skater carries a stick the length of the ice and hands it to the next teammate, who carries two sticks back, then three, and the first team with all its sticks in one place wins.
session_objectives: Fun day, Fun games incorporating skill combinations

title: Full Ice Batchko
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 24
description: Full Ice Batchko: Play a controlled scrimmage where each player gets only two touches before passing or shooting. Receiving on the backhand is one touch and moving it to the forehand is a second, so the puck must go. More than two touches stops play and the puck goes to the other team.
session_objectives: Fun day, Fun games incorporating skill combinations

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 25)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 25
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner with a puck and skate the lanes. Each lane has its own puck skill: narrow and wide movement, front toe drags, side toe drags, and dropping the puck into the skates and kicking it back up to the stick.
coaching_points: Get creative with different stickhandling moves.
session_objectives: Refine skating and puck control skills, Use of fun games to challenge skating skills, player creativity

title: Crossover Progression · Stride / Crossover Combo · Backward Crossover Progression
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 25
description: Crossover Progression: From the corner, players work through outside foot C-cuts, C-cut crossunders, exaggerated crossovers and full crossovers at higher speed. Stride / Crossover Combo: From the boards with pucks, players skate to the faceoff dot, pivot to backward to the far dot, pivot forward around the circle back to the dot, then pivot backward and return to the line. Backward Crossover Progression: From the corner, players work through outside foot C-cuts, backward crossovers and reaching backward crossovers.
coaching_points: Full knee bend and ankle flex, low centre of gravity, stick on the ice.
Head up, accelerate out of turns with quick feet.
Send the next player when the first reaches the far faceoff dot.
session_objectives: Refine skating and puck control skills, Use of fun games to challenge skating skills, player creativity

title: Combo Skate Pass/Shoot · Offensive Fakes · Shootout Competition
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 25
description: Combo Skate Pass/Shoot: O3 skates around the top of the circle, takes a pass from O2, makes an evasive move on the coach and shoots, then repeat the other way. Offensive Fakes: From the boards with pylons set as diagrammed, a player carries out, makes a move on a pylon and passes to the next player, using body fakes, stick fakes, fake inside go outside and fake outside go inside. Shootout Competition: Two lines at centre ice, one player standing with a puck and one on a knee; on the signal the carrier attacks the net while the other backchecks, and a backchecker who takes the puck becomes the attacker.
session_objectives: Refine skating and puck control skills, Use of fun games to challenge skating skills, player creativity

title: 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 25, 26
description: 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout: Players line up in two lines at centre. On the whistle both race to the net, each trying to win body position to receive a pass and shoot. Alternate offence and defence.
coaching_points: Quick start.
The attacker uses the body to block out the defender.
Stick on the ice, ready for a quick shot.
session_objectives: Refine skating and puck control skills, Use of fun games to challenge skating skills, player creativity

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 26)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 26
description: Warm Up: Players stickhandle all over the zone. On the whistle a coach skates in and checks players, shooting their pucks out of the zone. Checked players become checkers, and the last player with a puck wins. A coach stays with the goalie in the goal zone.
coaching_points: Head up, quick feet and protect the puck.
Move the puck quickly and skate to open space.
session_objectives: Offensive fakes, Shooting in motion, Checking skills, Net drive

title: Offensive Fakes · Shooting in Motion · Puck Control/Fakes
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 26
description: Offensive Fakes: After a coach demo, players practise puck back through the legs, toe drag, spin-o-rama, 360 move and heel to heel move, with O1 carrying across and dropping to O2, who carries across and drops to O3, and so on. Shooting in Motion: Players spread out practising wrist and backhand shots, then skate toward the boards and shoot on the move. Puck Control/Fakes: Players skate around circle one, fake the coach and shoot, using moves such as leaving the puck and going around, or attacking the triangle with the puck between the legs or under the stick.
coaching_points: Head up, shift weight and keep quick feet.
Accelerate after the fake.
Players must be moving when they release the puck.
session_objectives: Offensive fakes, Shooting in motion, Checking skills, Net drive

title: Assessing Checking Skills · Net Drive Progression · Net Drive – Tactical Level
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 26
description: Assessing Checking Skills: In a 1 on 0 with a backchecker, O and D start a stick length apart and race to the top of the circle on the whistle, where O takes a lead pass from the coach and D stays close and checks if possible. Net Drive Progression: At the technical level, players skate around a pylon protecting the puck. Net Drive – Tactical Level: A player from the corner gives and goes with the coach, then drives the net with speed against passive pressure from the coach.
coaching_points: Defensive side positioning, stops and starts, stick checks and quick feet.
Approach with speed, puck to the outside, build the wall and drive the far post.
Keep the feet moving and accelerate after the fake.
session_objectives: Offensive fakes, Shooting in motion, Checking skills, Net drive

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 27)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner with a puck and skate the lanes. Each lane has its own puck skill: open ice carry, three crossovers while stickhandling, heel C-cuts, and narrow and wide slalom with toe drags.
coaching_points: Get creative with different stickhandling moves.
session_objectives: Net drive, Fakes and Dekes

title: Net Drive - Technical Level · Puck Control · Net Drive - Tactical Level
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: Net Drive - Technical Level: Players skate around a pylon protecting the puck. Puck Control: From the boards, players skate into the puck control box and make a move on each cone in random order, then straddle the puck dots and stickhandle through them on the way back. Net Drive - Tactical Level: A player from the corner gives and goes with the coach, then drives the net with speed against passive pressure from the coach.
coaching_points: Approach with speed, puck to the outside, build the wall and drive the far post.
Head up, keep the feet moving and be creative.
Accelerate after the fake with a weight shift.
session_objectives: Net drive, Fakes and Dekes

title: 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout · Fakes and Dekes · Net Drive - Efficient Level
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27
description: 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout: On the whistle two players race to the net, each trying to win body position to take a pass and shoot, alternating offence and defence. Fakes and Dekes: After a coach demo, players practise puck back through the legs, toe drag, spin-o-rama, 360 move and heel to heel move, with O1 carrying across and dropping to O2, and so on. Net Drive - Efficient Level: D carries to the blue line, passes to O and defends 1 on 1, and O reads the gap, driving outside against a tight gap and through the middle against a loose one.
coaching_points: Quick start and use the body to block out the defender.
Stick on the ice, ready for a quick shot.
Head up, shift weight, quick feet and accelerate after the fake.
session_objectives: Net drive, Fakes and Dekes

title: Circle Relay – 3 on 3
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 27, 31
description: Circle Relay – 3 on 3: Three players from each side line up outside the blue line. On the whistle they skate around the circles and back out around a pylon. The coach dumps a puck in on the goalies and they play 3 on 3 until one side scores. Change the skating each time around the circle, such as forward, backward or pivots.
coaching_points: Quick feet and pressure the puck.
Defend man to man.
Attackers move to open space.
session_objectives: Net drive, Fakes and Dekes

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 28)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Warm Up: Players skate around the ice at quarter speed. On the whistle they stay in a tight space and move the puck quickly in every direction. On the next whistle they go back to quarter speed.
coaching_points: Quick feet and quick puck movement.
Use evasive moves with body, head and shoulder fakes.
session_objectives: Checking, Angling, Fakes and Dekes, Net drives

title: Checking Drill – Stick Checks · Fakes and Dekes · Net Drive
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Checking Drill – Stick Checks: Demonstrate the stick lift, press, poke and sweep check, then mark 1 on 1 zones with spray paint and have players play keep away focusing on checking. Fakes and Dekes: After a coach demo, players practise puck back through the legs, toe drag, spin-o-rama, 360 move and heel to heel move, with O1 carrying across and dropping to O2, and so on. Net Drive: Review net drive skills; a player leaves the blue line, skates across to take a pass from the opposite line and net drives around the coaches.
coaching_points: Quick stick, feet and hands with good body position in 30 second intervals.
Head up, shift weight and accelerate after the fake.
Alternate sides, enter the zone with speed and drive the far post.
Keep the feet moving and protect the puck.
session_objectives: Checking, Angling, Fakes and Dekes, Net drives

title: Checking – Angling · Checking – Gap Control · 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Checking – Angling: After a coach review, the coach dumps a puck in, O carries it out at half speed and D angles O into the boards and rides them out. Checking – Gap Control: After reviewing body position and gap, two lanes are spray painted and O skates side to side at half speed while D keeps a tight gap, first without and then with pucks. 1 on 1 Body Position Shootout: On the whistle two players race to the net, each trying to win body position to take a pass and shoot, alternating offence and defence.
coaching_points: Take away the middle with shoulders square to the attacker and stick on the ice.
One hand on the stick, outside shoulder to inside shoulder, controlled feet, eyes on the chest.
Quick start and use the body to block out the defender.
session_objectives: Checking, Angling, Fakes and Dekes, Net drives

title: Checking - Backcheck
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 28
description: Checking - Backcheck: The coach reviews backchecking technique. The attacker changes speeds while the defender stays close and holds body position. The coach simulates a pass, and players alternate roles.
coaching_points: Head on a swivel.
Take inside position with the stick on the ice.
Controlled skating.
session_objectives: Checking, Angling, Fakes and Dekes, Net drives

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 29)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner with a puck and skate the lanes. Each lane has its own puck skill: open ice carry, three crossovers while stickhandling, heel C-cuts, and narrow and wide slalom with toe drags.
coaching_points: Get creative with different stickhandling moves.
session_objectives: 2 on 1, 2 on 2, Angliing, Gap Control

title: 2 on 1 · Puck Control · 2 on 2
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: 2 on 1: On the coach's signal, D passes to an O on the near boards; the two O's make one pass before the blue line, then cross and attack 2 on 1 while D closes the gap after passing. Puck Control: From the boards, players skate into the puck control box and make a move on each cone in random order, then straddle the puck dots and stickhandle through them on the way back. 2 on 2: On the whistle the first O passes to the O on the faceoff dot, who can return a give and go or carry and headman the puck, while two D step out and defend 2 on 2.
coaching_points: Eye contact with the passer and a stick target on the ice.
Enter the zone with speed and support the puck carrier.
Communicate and read the D gap to cross or drive outside.
Head up and be creative.
session_objectives: 2 on 1, 2 on 2, Angliing, Gap Control

title: Angling · Checking – Gap Control · Scrimmage
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29
description: Angling: The coach dumps a puck into the O corner; D reads who has it and angles while O tries to carry to the blue line and D tries to angle and win it. Checking – Gap Control: After reviewing body position and gap, O skates side to side at half speed while D keeps a tight gap, first without and then with pucks. Scrimmage: Play continuously with quick changes on the whistle, stressing checking technique and defensive position while assessing offensive tactics such as give and go and headman passes.
coaching_points: Take away the middle with shoulders square to the attacker and stick on the ice.
One hand on the stick, outside shoulder to inside shoulder, controlled feet, eyes on the chest.
Offence moves the puck quickly; defence holds defensive side position.
session_objectives: 2 on 1, 2 on 2, Angliing, Gap Control

title: Shootout Competition
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 29, 30
description: Shootout Competition: Pucks are bunched in the centre circle. On the whistle the first player on each team grabs a puck and goes on a breakaway, continuing until they score, then the next player goes. The goalie can clear loose pucks.
coaching_points: The first team to have every player score wins; play best of three.
session_objectives: 2 on 1, 2 on 2, Angliing, Gap Control

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 30)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30, 31
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner with a puck and skate the lanes. Each lane has its own puck skill: puck through the legs from behind, hands together, hands wide, and side to side behind the body.
coaching_points: Get creative with different stickhandling moves.
session_objectives: 1 on 1, Fakes and Dekes, 2 on 2, Net drive, Stick checks

title: 1 on 1 · Fakes and Dekes · 2 on 2
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30
description: 1 on 1: Players line up on the blue line as diagrammed; the coach dumps a puck in, D skates backward, pivots at the hash marks and retrieves it, outlets to O anchored on the wall, and O skates around the top of the circle to attack 1 on 1 against D, who closes the gap. Fakes and Dekes: After a coach demo, players practise puck back through the legs, toe drag, spin-o-rama, 360 move and heel to heel move, with O1 carrying across and dropping to O2, and so on. 2 on 2: O1 and O2 skate the circle clockwise, cross in the high slot before the blue line with the option to exchange a pass, cross again at the blue line and attack, while D1 and D2 skate forward to the tops of the circles, pivot and defend 2 on 2.
coaching_points: Shoulder check, eye contact with the passer and a stick target on the ice.
Head up, shift weight and accelerate after the fake.
Communicate, control skate and get the timing right, going on the whistle.
session_objectives: 1 on 1, Fakes and Dekes, 2 on 2, Net drive, Stick checks

title: 1 on 0 with Backchecker · Checking Drill – Stick Checks · Net Drive
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 30
description: 1 on 0 with Backchecker: O and D start a stick length apart and race on the whistle to the blue line and the top of the circle, where O takes a lead pass from the coach and D stays close and checks if possible. Checking Drill – Stick Checks: Demonstrate the stick lift, press, poke and sweep check, then mark 1 on 1 zones with spray paint and play keep away focusing on checking. Net Drive: Review net drive skills; a player leaves the blue line, skates across to take a pass from the opposite line and net drives around the coaches.
coaching_points: Defensive side positioning, stops and starts, stick checks and quick feet.
Quick stick, feet and hands with good body position in 30 second intervals.
Alternate sides, enter the zone with speed and drive the far post.
Keep the feet moving and protect the puck.
session_objectives: 1 on 1, Fakes and Dekes, 2 on 2, Net drive, Stick checks

title: Shooting · Give and Go/Puck Control · Combo – Technical Skill Drill
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 31
description: Shooting: On the whistle, three players staggered in three lanes skate the length of the zone and shoot. Give and Go/Puck Control: From the boards on the signal, players give and go with both coaches, then weave pylons on the way back with the puck on the forehand only, forehand one-handed, inside the pylon off the stick and inside the pylon on the stick. Combo – Technical Skill Drill: O skates with stops and starts at the blue line and hash marks, pivots and skates backward, pivots open to take a pass, weaves the cones and shoots.
coaching_points: Space the lines, release quickly and get out of the way.
Give the goalie time to recover after each wave of three.
Give a target for the pass with head up and eye contact.
Finish with a quick shot on goal.
session_objectives: Shooting, Give and go, Puck support, Fakes and Dekes

title: Fakes/Dekes · Puck Support · Puck Control
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 31
description: Fakes/Dekes: A player carries out, makes a move on the cone and drives the net for a shot, alternating sides. Puck Support: Mark a box with spray paint or four pylons and place a stationary D in the middle; the two O's without the puck must give the carrier two options. Puck Control: From the corner, players skate into the puck control box and make a move on each cone in random order, then stickhandle through the puck control sticks on the way back.
coaching_points: Quick feet, quick release and follow up for the rebound.
No diagonal passes; supporting players must get open.
Head up and be creative.
session_objectives: Shooting, Give and go, Puck support, Fakes and Dekes

title: Warm Up (U9 Plan 32)
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: Warm Up: Players start in the corner with a puck and skate the lanes. Each lane has its own puck skill: side to side behind the body, one-leg edge control, two pucks, and two pucks with stick and feet.
coaching_points: Get creative with different stickhandling moves.
session_objectives: Puck Support, Fakes and Dekes, Puck Control

title: Montreal Drill · Pass with Accuracy · “pig in the Middle”
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: Montreal Drill: The puck goes O4 to O1, O1 to O2, O2 to O3 and O3 back to O4 in the slot, then players rotate. Pass with Accuracy: Players move laterally, giving and receiving the puck outside the cones. Pig in the Middle: In groups of four, three pass in a triangle while the fourth tries to intercept, and whoever turns it over goes to the middle.
coaching_points: Eyes on the target.
Always give a target.
Use deception.
session_objectives: Puck Support, Fakes and Dekes, Puck Control

title: Fakes/Dekes · Checking – Gap Control · Controlled Scrimmage
source_collection: Hockey Canada U9 Skills Development Program · Practice Plan 32
description: Fakes/Dekes: A player carries out, makes a move on the coach and drives the net for a shot, alternating sides. Checking – Gap Control: After reviewing body position and gap, O skates side to side at half speed while D keeps a tight gap, first without and then with pucks. Controlled Scrimmage: Focus on carrying out team tactics and assessing basic positioning.
coaching_points: Quick feet, quick release and follow up for the rebound.
One hand on the stick, outside shoulder to inside shoulder, controlled feet, eyes on the chest.
Players freeze on the whistle and the coach gives positioning feedback.
